test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 27 Feb 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: As of December 2020, how many fundamental duties are enumerated in the Constitution of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**11**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The original Constitution of India did not contain Fundamental Duties.
 
• Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• Initially, there were 10 Fundamental Duties enumerated in Article 51A of the Constitution.
 
• The 86th Amendment Act, 2002, added one more Fundamental Duty, raising the total to 11.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties:**

 
 
• Fundamental Duties are moral obligations of all citizens to help promote a spirit of patriotism and to uphold the unity of India.
 
• They are included in Part IV-A of the Constitution.
 
• The Fundamental Duties are not enforceable by law, but they are essential for the overall development of the country.
 
 
 
• **42nd Amendment Act, 1976:**
 
 
• Known as the "Mini Constitution" due to its wide-ranging impact.
 
• Introduced significant changes to the Constitution, including the addition of Fundamental Duties.
 
 
 
• **86th Amendment Act, 2002:**
 
 
• Made education a Fundamental Right for children aged 6 to 14 years under Article 21A.
 
• Added a new Fundamental Duty under Article 51A (k) which states that a parent or guardian must provide opportunities for education to their child or ward between the age of six and fourteen years.
 
 
 
• **Swaran Singh Committee:**
 
 
• Set up by the Government of India in 1976 to recommend changes to the Constitution.
 
• Its recommendations led to the inclusion of Fundamental Duties in the Constitution.
